summary: Phase A RETEST — all requested scenarios PASS. (D) Premium create flow via UI (admin login → Couple → partner → romantic → $50-$100 → 10 miles / 'Austin, TX' → when-find-sparks-button): results-loading visible, then spark-card-0 rendered in ~20s with NO 'Request failed (500)'. No red screen. Direct API verification POST /api/sparks/generate with Authorization: Bearer <admin> + X-Premium:1 + X-Guest-ID returned HTTP 200 with keys sparks[] and usage{used:3,limit:3}. The server.py:658 NameError (iteration_9) is FIXED (`usage = await usage_for(ident, cfg)` now assigned before use). (C) 402 flow: with free_spark_limit=0 and a fresh guest (localStorage cleared), the create flow auto-navigated to /premium?reason=limit (Premium screen rendered: 'DATE SPARK PREMIUM', 'Take Your Spark Further', 'Start Premium — 14 days free'); browser back then landed on /create/results showing results-limit=TRUE and results-premium-button=TRUE — both the auto-nav branch and the 'back' results-limit branch work as intended. (F) Console: ZERO 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' warnings across all three browser sessions (confirms results.tsx router.replace moved into useEffect). Deep-link GET /create/results with no draft → redirected to /create (final URL /create, no /results). (SETUP note) Scenario C initially surfaced 429 ('Taking a short breather — Too many new guest sessions from your network today') because the shared egress IP's guest_ids_per_ip_daily (20) was exhausted by prior iterations — raised to 200 for the duration of Scenario C only, then restored. FINAL: GET /api/admin/config confirms limits == {ip_hourly_cap:20, ip_daily_cap:80, guest_ids_per_ip_daily:20, premium_daily_cap:15, premium_monthly_cap:60} and free_spark_limit == 3. Total LLM generations consumed this run: 2 (1 direct API + 1 UI).
critical_code_review_comments: Scenario C needed a temp bump of guest_ids_per_ip_daily (20→200) because the shared egress IP had hit its daily guest-ID cap from prior iterations. Not a bug — just a shared-infra fact. Consider documenting that the test runner's IP is sticky across iterations so limit resets have to be mindful.

No red screens, no page errors across the run.
